Commentary.Commentary: So, Sri Lanka chasing an improbable task of winning this Test by chasing a record 361 runs for victory. They already lead  the two-match series 1-0. How will they approach it? Will they go for a win or take a defensive action and settle for a draw? Stay tuned for Sri Lanka's reply on the other side of the break.

Sri Lankan bowling was better but they lacked penetration in their attack. The pacers Suranga Lakmal, Lahiru Kumara and Vishwa Fernando were very wayward and failed to contain the Zimbabwean batsmen. Though they managed to pick wickets the run flow was constantly there. Lasith Embuldeniya did trouble the batsmen with his variations and by getting the ball to turn and bounce regularly but he lacked support from the other end.

Zimbabwe have set the target of 361 for the visitors to chase down in almost 96 overs. The hosts started their second essay by taking a lead off 113 and then contributions from Brendan Taylor, Sikandar Raza  and skipper Sean Williams took their lead over the 350-run mark. Taylor played some aggressive cricket on Day 4 along with Sikandar Raza.  The duo added 70 valuable runs to take any hope of Sri Lanka winning it. Sean Williams came out to bat despite suffering from flu and he did hang around with the tail to get to his fifty.
Wow! ZIMBABWE HAVE DECLARED! What a moment. Zimbabwe's innings have lasted just 1 ball on Day 5. How often do we see such type of declaration in Test cricket?

SIX! 50 for Sean Williams. It has been a brilliant innings from him. Full delivery on middle, Williams flicks it over square leg for a maximum. ZIMBABWE DECLARE ON 247/7! THEY HAVE A LEAD OF 360 RUNS!
We are all set to begin Day 5. The players are out in the middle. Sean Williams and Donald Tiripano will resume their batting for Zimbabwe. Suranga Lakmal will finish his over.
Pitch Report - Tino Mawoyo says that it is a Day 5 wicket. Adds that there are some areas where the balls have kept low. Mentions the spinners will come into play.

A warm welcome to Day 5 of the 2nd Test between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka at Harare. The hosts already have a lead of 354 and overnight declaration is one of the possibility that Zimbabwe will look for and go for the kill. The weather seems to be fine to begin but there are chances of rain later in the day. Sri Lanka will want that to continue and eke out a draw if not go for a win. The pitch has started to take turn and there is some uneven bounce as well. A few balls from the pacers are keeping low too. Will Zimbabwe declare or will Sri Lanka be happy to bowl the entire day? Or will the visitors come out to bat later in the day? Stay tuned for the action coming up shortly.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

So the hosts have a massive lead of 354 on a wicket which has demons of its own. The ball is gripping, turning and also staying low. Sri Lanka have a massive task in hand, forget about winning for a moment as saving this game will also be very difficult. What do we have in store for the final day of this Test? Can Zimbabwe pull of a stunning win or will Sri Lanka break their hearts? Will weather play spoilsport? To know all the answers for these questions join us on Friday, 31st January for Day 5 of this Test. There will be an early start at 0930 local (0730 GMT) with 98 overs expected to be bowled. Hope to see you then. Till then, cheers!

It was a decent enough day for the Sri Lankan bowlers but on a pitch which is getting difficult to bat on they will be a bit disappointed that they were unable to bundle out Zimbabwe under 300 and are staring at a lead in excess of 350. Embuldeniya looked the most threatening and scalped two wickets. Lahiru Kumara and Suranga Lakmal had one wicket a piece while Vishwa Fernando with two wickets impressed with his control. Their bowling duties might just be done here as one would think Zimbabwe won't bat tomorrow.

We had very little play on Day 4 but it belonged to the hosts. They started the day with a lead of 175 and have managed to balloon it past the 350-run mark and one will feel they have killed the possibility of Sri Lanka's win. Although the rain gods have complicated their chance of a win as well. The hosts have managed to get this lead with the help of Brendan Taylor's 67, along with crucial start from Sikandar Raza. Just when the hosts were losing their way, Sean Williams hung out there and steadied the ship on a pitch which is looking very tricky to bat on. He is still unbeaten on 47 and it will be interesting to see if the skipper bats further or declares overnight.

STUMPS ON DAY 4! So that is it from this frustrating day of cricket as rain played the role of an antagonist and annoyed all us cricketing fans and just when it stopped we managed to get in a few overs before we were struck with a double blow of bad light and rain which unfortunately was the end of the day.

UPDATE 1628 local (1428 GMT) - This is bad, really bad. Hate to be the bad news bearer but any further play looks really difficult here as rain has come back to add to injury and the covers are coming on. But let's keep our fingers crossed and hope we have a little bit of more action today.
Oh no! It has gone dark here and the umpires are not happy with the reading on the light meter so the players are off and the play gets stopped due to Bad Light now.
On off, Tiripano pushes it towards cover with soft hands and gets a single.
Short but down the leg side, Tiripano looks to pull but misses.
Donald Tiripano is the new man in.

OUT! Bowled! That is the end of Mutombodzi. Lakmal gets his first wicket of the innings. It is not the best of deliveries but Mutombodzi gets beaten for pace. It is on the leg stump, Tinotenda looks to flick but is late in his attempt to do so. The ball goes past him and rattles the leg pole. It is getting darker here and the hosts have lost their 7th wicket. Will they declare or do they want more runs here?
Back of a length on off, Mutombodzi pulls it with confidence in front of square on the off side and gets a couple.
Lakmal hits the deck hard, Williams pulls it towards mid-wicket for a single.
It is getting dark and the light meter is out now.
Good length ball on off, Mutombodzi looks to pull but the ball does not rise and gets an inside edge onto the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Back of a length on off, Williams pulls it wide of mid-wicket and gets a single. The lead now stands at 350.
Fuller on middle, Williams strokes it towards mid on and gets a run.
Good length delivery on off, Mutombodzi defends it towards cover with soft hands and gets a single.
Outside off on a length, Mutombodzi looks to pull but misses.
On off, Mutombodzi pulls it wide of mid-wicket and keeps the strike.
Fuller on middle, SW pushes it wide of mid on and gets to the other end.
Short ball around off, Williams pulls it but finds short mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, Mutombodzi taps it towards point and gets a single.
Back of a length around off, Williams pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Full on middle, Williams pushes it to mid on.
On the stumps, Mutombodzi blocks it.
Good length ball outside off, Mutombodzi looks to punch but gets a bottom edge which goes to the left of the keeper. Dickwella does well as he is wrong footed to stop the ball.
On off, defended by Mutombodzi.

Direct hit but Williams is in. Fuller on middle, Williams pushes it to mid on and calls for a quick single. Lakmal there gets down to take the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. Williams stretches and drags his bat down inside the crease. The umpire goes upstairs to check and replay shows Sean is in.
Run Out appeal taken upstairs. Williams looks to be in but one can never be sure about it when it is a direct hit.
Good length ball outside off, Williams looks to defend but misses.
On the pads, Williams looks to flick but the ball goes off the thigh pad fine down the leg side and they take two runs off leg byes.
Outside off, left alone by Mutombodzi to get through the over.
This time Mutombodzi defends it off the middle.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Mathews is the culprit and he should have taken that one to be fair. Good length delivery around off, Mutombodzi has a poke at it but the ball zips away and kisses the outside edge of his willow. The ball falls on its way to the right of first slip. Angelo Mathews gets down on that side and gets his fingers to it but fails to bask it in. Poor and lethargic effort from the experienced campaigner.
Once again Lakmal strays on the pads, Sean turns it to the on side for a single.
Full on the pads, Mutombodzi glances it to the leg side for a run.
On the pads, Williams looks to flick but misses, the ball clips his pads and goes to the leg side for a single.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl the first proper over of the session.
Length ball on off, Mutombodzi defends it.
Fuller on off, Mutombodzi squeezes it through covers and gets a couple.

Huge appeal for LBW but the umpire turns it down. Good length delivery on the pads, Mutombodzi looks to pull but misses and gets hit on the pads. He misses and there is a huge appeal for LBW but the umpire is unmoved. The pitching looked to be an issue.
Full and on the pads, Williams flicks it towards backward square leg and gets a single.

We are all set for the action to begin. The Sri Lankan players walk out to the field and are taking their position in the field. Sean Williams and Tinotenda Mutombodzi stride out to resume their innings. Vishwa Fernando to bowl out the remaining ball of his over.

UPDATE 1540 local (1340 GMT) - Covers are completely off and the Sri Lankan players are out doing some warm ups. The umpires have checked the playing area and it looks like we are all set for the action to begin in some time.

UPDATE 1520 local (1320 GMT) - We have a positive news for all the cricket fans. The rain has stopped and the covers are slowly coming off and to add cherry on top. There will be an inspection at 1540 local.

Update 1513 local (1313 GMT) - It appears that the rain has stopped and the groundsmen are out in the middle. They are trying their best to get the field ready for play. The conditions though are pretty gloomy and we will have to wait for the official confirmation. Stay tuned, we will keep you posted.
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

With rain coming around Zimbabwe would look to tweak their plan a bit and declare earlier than they would have liked and take a  couple of wickets before the close. Whereas, the Lankan lions will hope for Zimbabwe's declaration or bowling them out inside 400 and then look to chase the target down. Fingers crossed at the moment as it continues to pour steadily.  Good News! As I type THE RAIN HAS STOPPED! The umpires are seen with the ground staff. The groundsmen are rolling on the covers but the issue is there is a lot of water on the cover and also it is a bit dark out there. Let's hope that we can start the action quickly in this exciting Test.

So, the rain has failed to relent and the players take Tea. Zimbabwe would be ruing this break as they were going along nicely and now they will have to start it again as and when the game resumes. Fifty from Brendan Taylor and a fine partnership between skipper, Sean Williams and Sikandar Raza helped the hosts to extend their lead beyond 300. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, have kept themselves in the game by picking up wickets regularly.

Update 1425 Local (1225 GMT) - More bad news as the showers have got heavier in Harare and it seems like the players will take an early Tea break. Let's hope that play resumes shortly with the match poised finely in the balance.

Update 1345 Local (1145 GMT) - Oh, oh! As predicted just before the Lunch break, rain has interrupted the game and the umpires are calling the players off, or more precisely, the groundsmen on to cover the pitch. It looks like a drizzle and nothing else and hopefully we will resume shortly.
A slower yorker, landing wide outside off, Williams jams it out towards the off side.
Full ball on off to start the over by Fernando, pushed towards mid off by Williams.
Turning away from the batsman, Mutombodzi goes on the back foot to defend but it turns away from his bat.
Fires in a flatter full ball on off, probably an arm ball, Tinotenda defends it off his front foot.
Nicely tossed up ball outside off, spinning away, Mutombodzi stretches his front leg forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
Too full in length around leg, Williams sweeps it to deep square leg for a run.
Flatter and quicker on the pads, Williams tickles it behind square leg and his partner shows interest in a run. Sean sends him back.
Poor delivery and Lasith Embuldeniya gets away with it. Short and around leg, Williams turns to pull but finds backward square leg.
Fuller length delivery on middle and off, Mutombodzi stays back in defense. End of a successful over for Vishwa where he got lucky with a wicket.

DRINKS! What a time to take a wicket, just before the hour mark and Sri Lanka have got the breakthrough at the right time. Raza and Williams were going well and were amidst a 70-run stand but Fernando struck and that might prove to be a turning point as Sri Lanka will now be bowling at the lower order. They will try to limit the damage and restrict Zimbabwe's lead under 400. Here comes debutant Tinotenda Mutombodzi to face his first ball of this innings.

OUT! Given lbw and Sikandar Raza is not happy with it. We can understand the reason for that. Wait as we elaborate this wicket. Vishwa comes up with a pacey full delivery to which Raza tries a flick shot. He fails to put bat on ball and is rapped on the pads. The appeal is made and the finger goes up after a bit of a delay. Vishwa is pumped up after breaking the 70-run stand and Sikandar has to walk back. He's shaking his head. Here comes the replay and it clearly shows that the ball had pitched outside leg. Umpire Nitin Menon is having an odd bad day. Zimbabwe lose their sixth wicket and are effectively 334/6!
Length ball on middle and off, Williams taps it towards point and takes a single.
Length ball just outside off, left alone by Williams.
Good length ball on the off side, Raza dabs it towards the off side and takes a quick single.
Swing and a miss! Bouncer outside off, Raza looks to play the hook shot but misses it completely.
Last ball of the over and Raza rocks back to punch this flat delivery on off towards point for a single.
Another one which is quicker and flatter, Raza does well to block this one out onto the turf.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards the man at cover by Sikandar.
This time it is a bit quicker and outside off, Raza plays it towards the man at point.
Floated delivery and full on middle, Raza goes back and defends.
Missed out! A full toss outside off, Williams goes down on one knee and plays the sweep shot but finds the man at deep mid-wicket. Single taken.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and solidly blocks it towards short cover.
Good length ball on middle and off, Sikandar gets forward and defends it right under his watchful eyes.
Well bowled! Fernando senses the charge from the batsman and immediately shortens his length. Delivers it close to off and Raza does well to let it through.
Angling across the right-hander, around off on a length, Raza forces it off his back foot to short cover.
Slightly short this time, around off, Williams taps it down towards cover-point and pinches a single.
Williams misses out there! A half-volley outside off, Sean plays a lovely cover drive but finds the fielder.

Appeal for an lbw, not given as umpire Aleem Dar gestures it to be pitching outside the line of leg stump. A nicely flighted ball, Raza goes down to sweep but misses. He wears it on his back leg and they put in an unsuccessful appeal.
Very full and on off, Raza jams it out safely.
Walks forward with a full face of his bat and pushes it back to the bowler.
Bad line from Embuldeniya. Delivers a shortish ball around leg, Williams moves inside the crease and hits it to deep square leg for a single.
The bowler drags his length short and serves it outside off, Raza rocks back and slaps it to deep cover for a run.
Full and flighted on middle, it's flicked on the leg side but straight to short mid-wicket.

The bowler stops a certain boundary! Fuller length ball on off, Williams unveils a delightful straight drive but Fernando immediately goes down in his followthrough and stops the racing ball with his left hand.
Looks like a slower delivery. On a length and just outside off, Williams delays his shot a bit before pushing it out with an angled bat to cover-point.
A cracking cover drive once again from the bat of the Zimbabwean skipper. But this time he picks out the cover fielder.

FOUR! Unbelievable hands of Sean Williams. Also good eye to pick the line and length so early. There is width outside off and Sean picks it in a trice. Uses his lovely hands to reach out for it and crunches it through covers.
Fullish and angling in on off, Sean flicks it across the line but finds short mid-wicket.
Williams has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Dismissed! Time and again we have seen these two batsmen use their feet to good effect. Once again Raza wears his skates to dance down to the pitch of the ball and lifts it with the spin over mid off. It falls just inside the rope before crossing it.
Spinning down the leg side, Williams tries to flick but it takes a thin inside edge and runs down towards fine leg. A single is taken.
Very full and on middle, knocked down the ground towards mid on.
Turning back into the batsman from around off with some extra bounce, Sean turns it on the leg side but finds backward square leg.
Raza allows the ball to land as he guesses it to be the shorter one. It's short and Sikandar has cut it through cover-point for a run.
Full and flighted around off, Sikandar is on the front foot as he defends it watchfully.
Williams has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length and outside off, holding its line, Williams pushes inside the line and misses.
Beaten on the drive! Fernando serves it full and wide outside off, Sean goes for a big drive but fails to connect.
Good length delivery on middle, Raza gets on top of the bounce and turns it through square leg for a run.
Pitches it up and outside off, inviting the drive, Raza obliges, times his drive perfectly as well but picks out the cover fielder.
Short in length on middle to begin a new spell. It's pulled by Williams to deep square leg for a single.
Vishwa Fernando (13-5-28-1) is back on.
Allows the ball to spin back in and works it in front of square leg for a run. Easy going post Lunch for this pair, they have extended the lead to 315 runs!
Too full in length on middle, Williams pushes it past the bowler to mid on.
Fires a flatter delivery down the leg side, Sean tries to flick but misses.
50-run stand between the two! Once again this pair has been involved in a handy contribution. Shortish and on off, Raza punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Flatter and shorter on off, Raza cuts it from the back foot but finds point.
Tossed up ball around off, defended off the front foot by Raza.

Not in any control of his shot. Lakmal digs it short and lands it close to off, Raza jumps to pull but fails to middle his shot. It flies off the top edge and falls in no man's land at deep mid-wicket. There are a couple of fielders present in the deep but it evades them both.

Uppish but safe! Fullish ball around off, angling in and stopping a bit onto the batsman, Raza checks his push through the line and sends it aerially past the diving bowler. After that it safely rolls to mid off.

Edged but safe! Lakmal switches to over the wicket and dishes out an outswinger outside off. The length is full and Raza tries to play the cover drive. However, it takes the outer half and rolls to first slip. The fielder there makes a fine diving stop.
The line changes a bit from Lakmal. He serves it on a length and outside off, Williams steers it through point. He consciously stays away from the danger area while collecting a run.
Once again Lakmal speeds in and slants in a full ball on middle, Williams pushes it out with firm hands to covers.
Lakmal runs in from 'round the wicket and angles in a full ball on middle, Williams covers the line and drives it back to the bowler.
Fires it in flat and around off, Sikandar punches it from the crease to covers. Expensive over by Embuldeniya comes to a close.

Beauty to beat the bat! This pitch is very supportive for the spinners and time and again it has proved it. Nicely tossed up ball around off, Raza tries to play the line but it spins away to beat the outside edge. A good take by the keeper.
Smart batting by Sean! A couple of boundaries in the over and now he bunts a full ball to mid off for a quick run.

FOUR! Wow. Here goes Sean Williams again. He has flu but that's not showing in his batting. Once again Embuldeniya is too full in his length and Sean has no qualms in putting it through square leg. Zimbabwe continue to march!
Lunges to a full ball around off and defends it back watchfully.
FOUR! Thumped! Good shot from the captain. Williams sits down on one knee to fetch a full ball from outside off and then he sweeps it firmly in front of square leg for a cracking boundary.
Bouncer just outside off, Raza drops his hands and lets that ball go through to the keeper.
Good length ball outside off, Williams plays this one towards point and takes a single.
No ball! Overstepping by Lakmal! A very full ball on off, Williams plays it towards wide mid off.
Full ball on off, blocked out by Williams.
Full ball on middle and off, Raza plays this one down the ground past the bowler and they take a quick single. With this single, the lead is now 300 for Zimbabwe.
Good length ball on middle and off, pushed down to the man at mid off.
On the pads of Raza, he works this one towards the leg side.
Floated delivery outside off, out comes the reverse sweep but Williams does not connect. He gets hit on the pads but the line is also outside off. So, no chance for LBW.
Quicker and fuller this time on the off pole line, Williams blocks it out.
Lasith strays down the leg side, Williams flicks this one towards square leg for a couple.
Good bowling by Embuldeniya. He pitches this one in the rough but Williams prods forward and places this one towards cover.
Tossed up on off again, Williams pushes it towards mid off.
Floated on off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Lasith Embuldeniya to bowl now. 13-0-57-2, his figures so far.
Full delivery again, played back towards the right of Lakmal. Maiden for Lakmal.
Lakmal pushes this one fuller, Raza does well to get his bat down in time and places this towards mid on.
Back of a length ball on middle, pushed towards the man at cover off the back foot.
Fuller ball on off, pushed towards the man at cover.
Another one outside off, Sikandar shoulders arms.
Length ball outside off to start the over by Lakmal, Raza leaves it alone.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl the second over after the break. 12-4-13-0 are his figures so far.
Flatter one on middle again, pushed back straight towards the bowler by Williams and he gets through the first over post-Lunch safely.
This time flatter on middle and leg, blocked out.
Another one floated on off, pushed towards the cover region.
Floated on off, defended towards mid off.

Uppish but safe! Another floated delivery on off, again Raza goes for a similar stroke but this time chips it towards the wide mid off region. The fielder from mid off runs towards it but it falls safe. That might have pitched in the rough and that is why some extra bounce on that.

FOUR! Straightaway out of the blocks are Zimbabwe! Floated delivery outside off, Raza has driven this through the cover region and the ball trudges past the ropes. What a start to the session for them!
The Sri Lankan players are back out in the middle. Sean Williams and Sikandar Raza are out in the middle to resume their innings. Dhananjaya de Silva will start with the ball for the visitors.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Sean Williams who had been unwell has come out to bat and Sikandar Raza is there with him. The duo would hope that they continue to weather the storm and keep Zimbabwe on top. On the other hand, Sri Lanka will hope that they clean up the last 5 wickets quickly and cheaply. What will happen come the next session? We can see that the groundsmen are bringing on the covers as they are predicted rain to come soon. Will rain come and stop play? Join us for the afternoon session at 1240 local (1040 GMT).

All in all a good session for the visitors but in the context of the game, Zimbabwe are still on top. The Lankans came out with a plan and executed it to perfection. Lasith Embuldeniya was once again the main bowler as he picked up a couple of wickets and brought Sri Lanka back into the game. He kept on asking questions to the Zimbabwe batsmen who failed to find the answers. The day started with Chakabva edging one to the slips and then the wickets kept on falling at regular intervals. Masvaure threw his wicket away as he was run out while the concussion substitute for Kevin Kasuza, Timysen Maruma could not do much in the middle. In the end, Brendan Taylor, who was going along nicely and aggressively, was sent packing courtesy a poor umpiring decision. However, due to their brilliant work in the first innings, they are close to a 300-run lead and will now look to swell that even more and give the visitors a steep target to chase down.
Shortish delivery on off again, Raza rocks back and punches this off the back foot towards cover for a single. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
FOUR! Floated delivery on middle and off, Raza has just lofted this one over the mid on fielder and the ball goes into the fence on the bounce.
Flatter delivery on middle and off, defended onto the turf.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side for a single.
This time Embuldeniya bowls it a bit short, Williams defends the ball off the back foot.
Raza comes forward and drives this down the ground for a single.
Williams has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Brilliant shot by Williams! A bad delivery by de Silva, short of a length ball outside off, Williams rocks back and drives this one wonderfully through the cover region off the back foot for a boundary.
Williams now prods forward and defends this one towards the bowler.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg and the batters take a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
De Silva floats one outside off, Raza comes forward and blocks.
Tossed up delivery on off, blocked out.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg for a couple.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, defended by Williams.
Floated delivery outside off, Raza prods forward and looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge towards third man for a single.
Another one outside off, cut towards the man at point.
FOUR! What a shot! Floated delivery on off, Raza goes back and cuts this one through the cover-point region for a boundary.
Williams prods forward and defends this loopy delivery out solidly.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! A bad delivery by de Silva and Williams has put it away. Shortish delivery on middle, Williams goes back and pulls this one towards square leg for a boundary.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated delivery on middle and off, blocked out.
A shortish ball to start off with, Raza pulls it towards square leg for a couple.
Dhananjaya de Silva to roll his arm over. 4-2-17-0 are his figures so far.
FOUR! What a way to get off the mark! Full ball on off, Williams gets down and plays the square drive through the point region and bags a boundary.
Similar delivery, Williams punches it towards the man at cover.
Length ball on off, punched off the back foot towards the off side by Williams.
Sean Williams is out to bat. He was off the field on Day 3 due to flu and has come out to bat lower down the order today. He still looks unfit but has come out with his team in trouble here.

OUT! LBW! Brendan Taylor has to depart but he is very unhappy and that looks like a very harsh decision! Length ball on off, angling in towards Brendan Taylor. He looks to defend but fails to do so. The ball hits his pad and the Lankan players appeal. The umpire, Nitin Menon, raises his finger. Brendan Taylor starts walking back as there are no referrals here but he points the bat towards the umpire indicating he had nicked that. It also looked like it was going down the leg pole. Does not matter now! Zimbabwe have half the side back in the hut with that. Zimbabwe are effectively 264/5.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended.
FOUR! Creamed! Full ball on off, a half-volley, Taylor leans forward and drives this one through extra cover for a boundary.
Another one which is quicker and outside off, Raza plays it towards the man at point.
Floated on off, pushed towards cover.
Shortish outside off, played towards the man at point.
Now targets the middle pole with a quicker one, Raza stays strong and defends it.
Outside off, defended towards the off side.
Floated outside off, played towards sweeper cover for a single.
Back of a length ball on off, Raza blocks it off the back foot towards covers.
Length ball kept out off the back foot.
Taylor drives this full ball off the front foot and takes off for a quick single. The fielder there has a shy at the bowler'e end but misses it.

Short and on off once again, Taylor this time connects on the upper cut and ramps it off the face of the bat over the keeper. But lack of timing on it means that the slip fielder will mop it up. A couple taken.
EDGED BUT SAFE! Taylor looks to defend the length ball outside off but he gets an outside edge that drops short off the slip fielder. He did play it with soft hands.
Short ball and outside off, Taylor stands tall and looks to steer it over the keeper and the slip. He misses though in his attempt and the keeper does well to take it. A wide given.
Length ball outside off, Taylor pushes the ball through covers and takes an easy couple.
Flatter delivery on off, pushed down to long on for a single and Taylor will keep strike.
This time Taylor brings out the reverse sweep and plays this one towards third man. He gets a couple.
Embuldeniya bowls another one outside off, Taylor looks to guide this down to third man but edges it along the ground towards the slip cordon.
Floated on off, blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle, Taylor plays the paddle sweep but the fielder at short fine leg does well to stop it.
Wonderful shot but just a couple! He has driven this full ball wonderfully towards cover for a couple.
FOUR BYES! Down the leg side, full ball, Raza looks to tickle it fine down the leg side but misses. Dickwella misses it too and the ball goes into the fine leg fence.
Swing and a miss! Good length ball outside off, Raza goes down on one knee and looks for a square drive but he misses it completely.
Another one on middle and off, Raza defends this off the back foot.
Length ball on off, punched towards the off side off the back foot.
Appeal but turned down! Length ball on middle, angling in. Taylor looks to flick it down the leg side but the ball goes off the pads towards fine leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off again, guided down towards third man.

What a beauty! Embuldeniya is in the groove! Floated delivery just outside off, Raza looks to have a poke at it but the ball turns away and beats the outside edge of his bat. Some serious turn there and that might have interested Raza too.
Floated delivery outside off, Taylor pushes it towards point for a single.
Another one which is quick in speed and short by Embuldeniya, this time it is pushed towards long off by Raza.
Shortish ball outside off, pushed towards cover off the back foot for a single.
Taylor keeps the strike off the last ball of the over. He flicks the length ball off his pads towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Back of a length ball on off, Taylor pushes it to covers.
Length ball on the pads, Raza tucks it towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Back of a length ball on off, Raza stays tall and punches the ball to covers.
Full and angled on middle and leg, Raza flicks it off the pads to mid-wicket.

In the air... But safe. Kumara has the opportunity there but he fails. Taylor is a bit tentative there. Kumara lands it on a length and on off, Taylor is on the back foot as he pushes the ball straight back towards the bowler. Kumara there stretches his left hand but the ball goes past him towards long off. The batsmen take a run.
Lahiru Kumara to bowl now.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on off, pushed towards the cover region.
Sikandar Raza, the star of the match so far, walks out to bat now.

OUT! STUMPED! Maruma has to depart! The session and the game now tilting towards the Lankans. Floated delivery outside off, Embuldeniya again gets the ball to spin away from the right-handed Maruma. He prods forward in an attempt to defend but is beaten by the turn. The ball is collected by Niroshan Dickwella and he whips the bails off in a flash as Maruma loses his balance. The leg umpire refers it upstairs and the replays find him short. Blows in quick succession for Zimbabwe and they have been pushed back by the Lankans.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Floated delivery outside, it pitches and turns away. Maruma leaves it alone.

50 up for Brendan Taylor! He has been fantastic today and this is his 10th Test half ton. Floated ball on off, pushed towards cover for a single by Taylor to get to this milestone. He will be looking to get to three figures from here.
Length delivery on middle and off, Maruma looks to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge and onto the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, left alone.
Full ball on off, defended by Maruma.
Pushed down to long on for a single.
SIX! Super shot by Brendan Taylor! Good length ball on middle and leg, Taylor has lofted that one over the long on region for a biggie.
The ball has struck the batsman hard on his hand. The fielding side is asking the question. The umpire decides the batsman is not out.
Shortish delivery on middle, punched down to long on for a single.
Another one which is tossed up outside off, Brendan prods forward and defends it towards the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle and off, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Up and over! Floated delivery on middle and off, Taylor lofts this one straight over the bowler's head and the ball crosses the ropes on the bounce.
Length ball angled outside off, Maruma does not fiddle with it.
Length ball angled on off, Maruma stays on the back foot and punches the ball towards covers.
Back of a length ball on off, Maruma taps it off the outside half off the bat towards gully who dives to his right and fields it.
Full once again and tailing back in too, Maruma keeps it out off the front foot.
Length ball angled across Maruma, he lets it be.
Full ball on off, Maruma blocks it right under his eyes.
Outside off, pitches and turns away. Taylor leaves it alone.
Taylor again prods forward and defends this floated delivery towards the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, defended off the front foot.
Timycen Maruma is the new man in. He is the subsitute for the injured Kevin Kasuza who was concussed while fielding at short leg yesterday.

OUT! RUN OUT! A quicker delivery just near the leg pole line, Masvaure looks to make room and guide it down to third man but gets an inside edge which goes towards fine leg. Dhananjaya de Silva gives it the chase. The batters take an easy single but Masvaure wants two. Taylor is not even looking at Prince and Masvaure is halfway down the track. However, de Silva spots that and throws the ball towards the non-striker's end. Masvaure turns back and puts in a dive but Embuldeniya collects the ball and whips the bails off. It looks out to the naked eye but the umpire wants to confirm it and goes upstairs. Replays roll in to show that Masvaure is well short despite his dive. He has to walk back and he is dejected. Zimbabwe are effectively 224/3.
Run out appeal! This looks out to the naked eye and yes, the replays confirm it. Masvaure has to walk back.
Flatter one on the pads, worked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full ball on off, blocked off the front foot towards covers.
Another full ball on off, Masvaure drives it to find mid off.
Full and angled into the off pole, Masvaure looks to defend it with an angled bat only to get a bottom edge that falls near the off stump and rolls behind towards first slip.
Another ball which is bowled on the length and around off, Masvaure pushes it off the front foot towards covers.
Length ball around off, Masvaure stands tall and keeps the ball out to the off side.
Yorker spot on! Fernando targets the sumps and gets it right in the blockhole. Masvaure does well to dig it at the last instance.
Flatter one on middle, Masvaure pushes it towards mid on for a single.

Great work by Kumara! Tossed up delivery on middle and off, flicked towards the mid-wicket region. The ball is trudging towards the fence but Kumara does well to keep the ball in play and the batters take three.
Tossed up on off, pushed down to long on for a single.
Floated delivery on middle and off, swept towards square leg for a single.

DROPPED! Vishwa Fernando is the culprit! However that was a very difficult catch. Floated delivery on off, Taylor looks to go over the long off region but does not time it well. The ball goes high and Vishwa Fernando gives it a chase running backwards. He gets to the ball, also gets two hands to it but the ball pops out and he tumbles onto the ground as well. The backup fielder mops it up and allows the batters to take a couple. Taylor gets a life and he will be looking to make the most of it.

Loud appeal or a desperate one, however it is turned down! Floated delivery outside off, it turns in. Taylor looks to defend but the ball hits his pads and the Lankan players appeal only for the umpire to turn it down. Impact looks to be outside off to the naked eye.

DRINKS BREAK! 1 wicket lost but Zimbabwe have scored 39 runs in the first hour of play as well. Neither side will be too disappointed but with Taylor and Masvaure both set at the crease, Zimbabwe will definitely be the happier side. If the Lankans want to put the pressure back on the hosts, they need wickets and that too in a bulk. The skies are cloudy and there is a chance of rain too. Let's hope for the best though! Lasith Embuldeniya to inaugurate this hour.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg for a single.

Woah! What was Taylor trying to do there? Bouncer down the leg side, Taylor initially looks to duck but then looks to go for the upper cut and misses it. There was a high chance he could have lost his wicket there, that too very cheaply.
Length ball on off, Taylor punches it towards cover.
Fernando goes fuller again, driven towards the man at mid on.
Bouncer on off, Taylor does well to sway away from it.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards mid on.

OH! Nearly a chop on! Masvaure backs away to this length ball on off and looks to steers it down to third man. The ball comes in with the angle and takes the bottom edge only to hit the boots of Prince. The ball rolls towards the keeper past the off stump.
Bumper on middle and leg, Masvaure is happy to duck under it.

FOUR! Kumara is guilty there. He bowls one on the pads of Masvaure. Prince just flicks it uppishly through square leg. There are shouts of 'catch it' but there is no one there. The ball rolls to the fence easily.
Length ball outside off, Prine plays the cover drive but finds the fielder.
Full and angled on leg, Taylor flicks it off his pads towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Taylor once again starts the over with a boundary. Kumara goes short and angles one away from the right-hander. Taylor just frees his arms and cuts it through point to fetch a boundary.
Once again slightly back of a length, Prince drives it straight to cover-point.
Short and outside off, Masvaure cuts it but finds point.
Length ball down the leg side, Taylor helps it to fine leg and gets to the other end.
Length ball on off, Taylor defends it off the front foot.
Full and angled in to the pads, Taylor flicks it towards square leg.

FOUR! That is smashed. Taylor is not going to hold himself back. Fernando goes full and on middle, Taylor flicks it uppishly and gets it over the mid-wicket fielder. The ball rolls behind for a boundary. The lead is now 203!
Full ball on off, driven towards the cover region but straight to the man.
Full ball on middle and off, Masvaure prods forward and defends presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Length ball on middle and leg, Masvaure looks to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge and onto the pads.
Fuller ball on off, driven towards mid on.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side by Masvaure.
Lahiru Kumara comes on to bowl now. 4-1-10-0, his figures so far.
Another one outside off, Taylor shoulders arms.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Another good length ball on middle and off, defended into the ground. Much better technique now by Taylor in defending these out.
Outside off, played towards point.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended off the front foot.

EDGED AND FOUR! Length ball just outside off, Taylor looks to drive at it but the ball goes off the inside edge and rolls into the fine leg fence. Taylor could have easily chopped that on but he survives again.
Bouncer on middle and leg, Masvaure ducks under it.
On the pads, flicked towards square leg for nothing.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
This time down the leg side, worked towards square leg for a single.
Almost! Length ball angling in towards Taylor, he looks to defend but one of his hand comes off the handle and the ball lobs off the top half towards square leg but lands just short of the man there.
Good length ball on off, defended back towards the bowler.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side.
Length ball on off, Masvaure punches this one towards the man at cover-point.
Beaten! A loose shot by Masvaure! Good length ball on off, Masvaure looks to go for the expansive cover drive but the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Length ball on middle and off, defended towards the cover region.
On the pads of Masvaure, he flicks this one towards the man at mid-wicket.
Outside off, left alone by Masvaure.
Length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot once again by Taylor.
Fullish ball on middle and off, defended towards the point region.
Back of a length ball on middle, punched towards covers off the back foot for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Confusion! This is the last thing that Zimbabwe would want. Masvaure is half way down the ground there and then has to head back quickly. Prince drives this full ball back past the bowler and takes off for a run. The fielder from mid off runs to his left and fields it. Taylor is ball watching at the bowler's end and later realizes that Prince is halfway down. He then sends his partner back. The fielder has a shy at the keeper's end but he misses it and Masvaure makes it easily. Lucky escape!
Full and angling into the pads of Masvaure. He goes for the flick only to miss it. The ball hits the pads and rolls towards the leg side.
Another full ball angling on the pads, Taylor flicks it off his pads towards fine leg and gets two. Once again, Lakmal fields it at fine leg.

Full and angling down the leg side, Taylor comes inside the line and looks to flick it but misses it. The ball hits the pads and rolls towards fine leg. Lakmal from deep square leg runs to his right and mops it up. Two leg byes given.
Full and on off, Taylor blocks it off the front foot towards covers.
The batsman has been struck on the pads as he looked to play that off the front foot.
Full and angling on middle and leg, Taylor looks to flick it but the ball takes the inside edge and hits the pads to roll towards square leg.
Full and angling on middle, Taylor pushes it off the front foot towards mid on.
Vishwa Fernando comes on to bowl for the first time on Day 4. His figures so far, 5-2-9-1.
Length ball coming into  the off stump, Prince blocks it off the front foot and keeps it out towards covers.

That is nasty! Masvaure is seen wanting there. Lakmal goes short and it is well-directed too. Masvaure goes for the pull but takes his eyes off the ball and in the process misses it. The ball hits the helmet and lobs towards the point fielder who takes the catch and appeals. The umpire is unmoved there.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Back of a length ball on off, Prince defends it off the front foot towards covers.
Length delivery coming in with the angle, Prince defends it off the front foot towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball outside off, Masvaure blocks it off the back foot towards covers.
Shortish ball by Embuldeniiya. Taylor rocks back and defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Floated delivery on off, Taylor gets down on one knee and reverse sweeps it past the short third man fielder for another boundary. Aggressive batting by Taylor.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Inspection of the ball now. The Sri Lankans think that there is some problem with the ball and they hand it to the umpire. The umpire checks it and returns it to Embuldeniya saying that the ball is fine and it is good to continue.
FOUR! Wonderfully done! Tossed up delivery outside off, this time Taylor does not leave it alone and guides it fine down to the third man fence for a boundary.
Similar delivery, Taylor shoulders arms again.
Floated delivery outside off, it pitches and turns away. Taylor leaves this one alone.
Length ball by Lakmal, Masvaure defends this one towards the off side off the back foot.
Fuller and attacking the off pole, Prince does well to block it out.
Another good length ball, this time closer to the off pole, angling in. It is blocked out towards the off side.
This time it is outside off, Masvaure defends this one towards cover-point.
Good length ball around the off pole line, angling in. Defended towards the off side by Masvaure.
Length ball on middle and leg, pushed back towards the bowler.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Taylor is off the mark. He gets a full ball on middle and leg, Taylor goes for the sweep and connects well and the ball rolls towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Tossed up on middle and Taylor comes on the front foot and smothers the spin there.
Brendan Taylor is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Early breakthrough for the Lankans on Day 4. This is what they would have wanted. Embuldeniya is the man to provide it. Embuldeniya floats one around off, it pitches and turns away. Chakabva goes at it lazily with soft hands only for the ball to take the outside edge. It flies towards first slip where Kusal Mendis accepts it gleefully. Sri Lanka would now look to push the Zimbabwe batsmen on the back foot by striking at regular intervals. Can they do it?
Another tossed up ball on middle and Chakabva is on the back foot as he plays it solidly.
Tossed up on middle, Chakabva pushes it back to the bowler off the front foot.
Length ball on off, Masvaure defends this one towards the off side. Maiden for Lakmal and he will look to continue this.
On the pads once again, flicked towards the man at square leg.

First time that the bowler has found the edge of the bat today. Length ball just outside off, angling in. Masvaure looks to defend but the ball goes off the outer half off the bat towards the man at gully on the bounce.
Lakmal now bowls a good length ball on middle and off, it is pushed down to the man at mid on.
This time on the pads by Lakmal, Masvaure works this one towards the leg side.
Length ball on middle and off, angling in. Masvaure defends it back towards the bowler.
Slightly shorter and on middle, Chakabva pushes it off the back foot towards the off side.

Floated on off, Masvaure drives it straight down the ground. The bowler dives to his left in his followthrough but he fails to field it cleanly. The ball rolls towards mid off and the batsmen take a single.
Tossed up around middle and off, Prince drives it towards the cover region.
Once again pushed quicker on off, Prince blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up ball outside off. Masvaure comes on the front foot and blocks it off the front foot.
Floated delivery on off, Chakabva comes on the front foot and pushes it towards covers for a run.
Lasith Embuldeniya to bowl from the other end.
BEATEN! Kumara starts with a full ball outside off, Masvaure goes for the forward push but without feet movement and the ball sneaks past the outside edge off the bat. Lazy from Prince there.

We are about to begin Day 4 and the morning session will be crucial for both the teams. Zimbabwe are effectively 175/1 and their two overnight batsmen, Regis Chakabva and Prince Masvaure will resume their innings. Lahiru Kumara will start off the proceedings for the day with one ball remaining of his last over.

Pitch report - Tino Mawayo is down for the pitch report. He says that on the golf course end, only 6 wickets have fallen and that is a very interesting thing as on the Club End, there is very thick, almost root like grass on the surface. 14 wickets have fallen on that end off which 12 have gone to the spinners. Adds it will especially trouble the left-handers. Ends by saying that the conditions are good for cricket right now but it seems that rain might come in later.

Hello and welcome to the fourth day of the second Test match between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka. This can prove to be the most pivotal day in the Test and it might as well decide who will win this match. In a surprising turn of events, Zimbabwe have turned up against the Lankans and have given them a run for their money. Right now, the hosts have a lead of 175 runs while also having 9 wickets in hand. On Day 3, Sikandar Raza ran riot as he destroyed the Sri Lankan batting line up by taking 7 wickets. On Day 4, Zimbabwe will be looking to maximize their lead and give the Lankans a hefty target to chase down. As for Sri Lanka, they would like to take wickets in a heap and put pressure on the hosts. An intriguing day awaits!
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

With 9 wickets still in the pocket for the hosts, they would look to play an aggressive brand of cricket and extend the lead beyond Sri Lanka's reach. On the other hand, Sri Lanka will hope that the morning session works in their favour and they get back in control of this Test by taking wickets in a heap. Day 4 promises to be a cracker as both teams will look to edge each other out. With early stumps on Day 3, play will start 25 minutes early. On Day 4, Thursday, the action will begin at 0935 local (0735 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Earlier in the day, Zimbabwe were all over Sri Lanka as Sikandar Raza blew them away by taking 7 wickets. The Zimbabwe bowling attack kept the Sri Lankan batsmen quiet and forced them to take risks. The credit also goes to the Zimbabwe pacers who bowled a probing line and length and choked the run flow. Apart from the 84-run stand between Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva, other batsmen failed to support Angelo Mathews in the middle. With pressure building and just the tail left to bat, Mathews fell after a well-fought fifty, his 35th in this format. Zimbabwe got a handy lead of 113 to play with and they capitalized on it by extending it to 175 by the end of Day 3.

Talking of the Sri Lankan bowling, they were a bit haywire with their lines and lengths. They kept on bowling outside off which did not trouble the Zimbabwe batters at all. Vishwa Fernando was the pick of the bowlers for the visitors as he took a wicket in his five overs and bowled tidy lines. It will be interesting to see what will happen on Day 4 with Zimbabwe batting well in their home conditions and the Lankans coming out fresh after a break.

After bowling Sri Lanka out in the extended second session, Zimbabwe came out to bat with a lot of intent after the Tea Break. The Zimbabwe openers, Prince Masvaure and Craig Ervine started the innings watchfully. Playing each and every ball on its merit. But Craig Ervine's stay at the crease was cut short as he edged one to the keeper. However, after that, the duo of Masvaure and Chakabva weathered the storm and kept the game control in Zimbabwe's hand until the storm literally came in and no more play was possible.
Yes, that will be it! The umpires have called for Stumps on Day 3 with rain interrupting play. It has been a good day of cricket and Zimbabwe will be the happier side going into Day 4.

Update 1445 Local (1645 GMT) - Oh, oh! Bad news is here as the dark clouds have started doing its work and rain has started to pour down. The groundsmen predicted it early on and were ready with the covers and now they are rushing with them to spread it across the pitch.

Good fielding! Dhananjaya de Silva is the man! Quicker delivery outside off, Chakabva plays this one towards cover-point. The ball is racing to the fence but de Silva chases it and keeps the ball in play. The batters take three runs.
On middle and leg, defended back towards the bowler.
Length ball just outside the off stump, near the fifth pole line, Chakabva makes a confident leave.
On middle and leg, worked towards the man at mid on.
